title: The Shield of Love: Protecting Your Child from Screens and Nurturing Yourself
summary:
Imagine this warm scene with me: your infant sleeps peacefully in their room, and you are enjoying rare moments of quiet. Suddenly, one of your phones lights up, or the sound of a video rises from the living room. In this early stage of your child's life, every interaction, every touch, and every real sound forms a fundamental building block in their rapidly developing brain. It is a golden period for direct human connection and sensory play that no digital device can replace.

Global guidelines indicate that infants and children up to one year old do not benefit from screen time; rather, real interactions are the fuel for their cognitive and emotional growth. Even if a short, high-quality video sometimes seems harmless, it does not replace the importance of play, movement, reading, and sufficient sleep. Content quality, family needs, and shared participation in media use are keys to navigating the digital world, always prioritizing real-life experiences that enrich your little one's world.

And because caring for your child begins with caring for yourselves, remember that your mental health is your first shield. Distinguishing between transient fatigue and postpartum depression is crucial. Do not hesitate to seek support and share roles as a couple. These practical steps not only protect you from burnout and chronic stress but also give you the strength and calm needed to provide the best care and love for your child, making the parenting journey an experience full of warmth and security.
